text:
alex: did a focused perf + flamegraph pass on the dedicated pool that hit the regression earlier today. attaching quick notes.
maria: nice, was this CPU-only (perf) or an nsys/GPU trace?
alex: CPU-only perf. i ran `perf record -F 99 -g -- /opt/redwood/bin/inference_server --cfg ded-small` then `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded` -> flamegraph.svg
chris: any obvious hot C kernels or mostly Python?
alex: mixed. the flame shows two big stacks: one is tokenization path in our python tokenizer (PyUnicode_Decode... -> tokenize_bytes -> Tokenizer.segment), second is BatchScheduler::pop_and_dispatch -> schedule_batch -> holding GIL while doing input prep. annotated sample:
```
PyEval_EvalFrameDefault
Tokenizer.segment
Tokenizer._byte_decode
Batcher::schedule
PyThread_acquire_lock
```
sam: so GIL is the limiter for batching thread? that matches the latency spikes we saw under 150qps load.
jordan: can you paste the flame snippet or top folded stacks?
alex: pasted top stacks (folded lines):
"PyEval_EvalFrameDefault;Tokenizer._byte_decode;Tokenizer.segment;batcher.execute;BatchScheduler::pop_and_dispatch  2345"
"BatchScheduler::pop_and_dispatch;Batcher::schedule;PyEval_EvalFrameDefault  1870"
perf-bot: automated note: perf sample count = 42100, contours saved to s3://redwood-perf/1859502467/
maria: hmm token decode in Python -> high iso time. we shipped a micro-optim that added an extra .decode() path last week. could be the culprit.
chris: also seeing a kernel selection churn: short-lived kernels being picked then fallback to slower non-quantized kernels when seq len variance is high. that could amplify CPU prep cost since we reserialize inputs.
alex: hypothesis: extra decode + Python-level input validation increases GIL hold times, which blocks batcher threads. blocked batcher means smaller effective batches -> runtime picks smaller kernels -> worse throughput.
sam: actionable checklist?
alex: 1) revert the decode micro-path on a canary build and rerun perf (quick). 2) add a perf counter that tags time spent under GIL in batcher threads. 3) run a low-overhead C-extension tokenizer (release GIL) on a sample workload to measure delta. 4) tweak batching heuristic: prefer waiting 5ms more for queue depth to stabilize to avoid kernel churn.
jordan: i can run the canary and the C-ext test on ded-staging, ping me if you want me to run later today.
maria: also add an eval to watch model kernel selection TTL; maybe we can cache kernel choice for N seconds when seq-length distribution is similar to avoid repeated recompile/selection.
alex: noted. i'll open a small PR for the revert + perf mark, and create an infra job to produce flamegraphs automatically after each canary deploy.
chris: one more tip: use `perf record -e cpu-clock -g` to reduce noise from SYS calls. i got cleaner stacks that pinpointed PyUnicode_Decode.
alex: thanks — i'll run both and post results here. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: job 1859502467-flame-automation created -> https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/1859502467
sam: +1 on the nudge to C-ext tokenizer. if delta is big we push as hotfix and enable in dedicated pools only.
alex: will follow up with numbers in this thread.
